content: The Medications for Opioid Use Disorder (MOUD) study investigated the outcomes of various treatment approaches for individuals with opioid use disorder (OUD). This research provides critical insights into the effectiveness of these treatments. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is actively engaged in efforts to prevent overdoses and mitigate harms associated with substance use. Their initiatives and highlights of ongoing work were last updated on February 21, 2024. The CDC offers access to comprehensive data resources, including dashboards that display fatal and nonfatal overdose statistics, as well as maps showing pharmacy dispensing rates. These resources were updated on May 8, 2024. Polysubstance overdose refers to situations where an individual experiences an overdose due to exposure to multiple drugs, either knowingly or unknowingly. This phenomenon was last addressed by the CDC on May 8, 2024. For healthcare providers, the CDC provides a range of resources focused on overdose prevention, including guidance on pain management, opioid use, and opioid use disorder. These resources were updated on May 7, 2024. The 2022 CDC Clinical Practice Guideline offers a detailed framework for prescribing opioids for pain management. This guideline aims to ensure safe and effective opioid prescribing practices and was last reviewed on May 7, 2024. The CDC also provides training programs for clinicians, covering topics such as pain management, opioid use disorder, naloxone administration, and substance use disorders. These training resources were updated on May 7, 2024. The Overdose Data to Action program serves as a central hub for information and resources related to overdose prevention. This program was last updated on May 2, 2024. The Drug-Free Communities (DFC) program, supported by the CDC, offers resources and information aimed at fostering drug-free environments. This program was last updated on May 8, 2024. Xylazine, a non-opioid sedative and tranquilizer, is not approved for human use. The CDC provides information on this substance to raise awareness about its risks. This information was last updated on May 8, 2024. Public health professionals can access a variety of resources for overdose prevention and intervention through the CDC. These resources were last updated on May 6, 2024. The CDC is dedicated to addressing health inequities and promoting health equity in the context of drug overdose prevention. Their commitment to this goal was last highlighted on March 19, 2024. The Overdose Resource Exchange (ORE) serves as a platform for sharing resources related to overdose prevention. This exchange was last updated on April 30, 2024. The CDC provides information on strategies and partnerships for overdose prevention, tailored for healthcare professionals. These resources were last updated on May 8, 2024.
